mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 5% and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% and 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines for 3 months and 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 2% and 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is below 3% YoY, this combination signals a tightening monetary policy without severe inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL YoY < 3% and 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases for 3 months and 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) also decline, this interaction signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS declines
failure_condition: If HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS declines and 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in one month, this signals a hawkish policy shift, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
